SeriesLinearAlgAccessor::svd_vh¶

Back to SeriesLinearAlgAccessor API Reference

Signatures¶

Series SeriesLinearAlgAccessor::svd_vh(bool full_matrices = true) const
Series SeriesLinearAlgProxy::svd_vh(bool full_matrices = true) const

What It Does¶

svd_vh() returns conjugate-transposed right singular vectors from A = U diag(S) Vh. Each row identifies an orthonormal input-space direction; A maps it to the matching column of U, scaled by the corresponding singular value.

Use svd_vh() when the task needs only principal directions in the input space: feature directions, right-null-space analysis, or projection of input coordinates. Use joint svd() when those rows must remain paired with their singular values or output directions.

Calling Styles And Which One To Use¶

auto direct = matrix.linearalg.svd_vh(false);    // accessor spelling
auto proxied = matrix.linearalg().svd_vh(false); // unary proxy spelling

Both expressions read the same matrix. SeriesLinearAlgProxy is only the temporary object returned by linearalg(); it does not mean “proxy data” and does not change the decomposition. Prefer the shorter direct spelling. SVD is unary, so no peer should be bound through linearalg(other).

Directions Presented As Rows¶

The h matters: directions are rows of Vh, not columns of V. For real inputs this is an ordinary transpose; for complex inputs it also conjugates. This orientation allows diag(S) Vh to appear directly in reconstruction.

Parameter And Shape¶

For [...,m,n] and k=min(m,n), full mode returns [...,n,n]; reduced mode returns [...,k,n].

Returns¶

Series Right singular directions stored row-wise. The same coordinated component is available as .vh on the result of svd().

Gradient¶

Use reduced mode for reverse differentiation. Repeated singular values make individual rows non-unique, and near ties can produce large vector gradients.

Examples¶

Example 1. A wide matrix shows why reduced and full Vh differ.

auto wide = pluss::make_series({{3.0, 0.0, 0.0}, {0.0, 2.0, 0.0}});
std::cout << "reduced=" << wide.linearalg.svd_vh(false) << "\n";
std::cout << "full=" << wide.linearalg.svd_vh(true) << "\n";

Output¶

reduced=pluss::Series(shape=[2,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 0, 0],
  [0, 1, 0]]
full=pluss::Series(shape=[3,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=9, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 0, 0],
  [0, 1, 0],
  [0, 0, 1]]

The extra full-mode row spans the right null space: the input direction that this 2 x 3 map sends to zero.

Example 2. Rows of reduced Vh are orthonormal.

auto matrix = pluss::make_series({{3.0, 1.0}, {1.0, 3.0}});
auto vh = matrix.linearalg.svd_vh(false);
std::cout << vh.linearalg.mm(vh.transpose(0, 1)) << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 4.2664216e-17],
  [4.2664216e-17, 1]]

Example 3. Reduced-mode singular directions participate in reverse mode.

auto matrix = pluss::make_series({{3.0, 1.0}, {0.0, 2.0}});
matrix.tracks_slope_(true);
matrix.linearalg.svd_vh(false).sum().reverse();
std::cout << matrix.sensitivity() << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[[0.25407734, -0.32667087],
  [-0.14518705, -0.21778058]]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • Rows, not columns, are the right singular directions.

  • Signs and bases inside repeated-value subspaces are not unique.

  • Pair this output with S and U produced using the same mode.

  • Full mode is not supported by reverse mode.

Summary¶

Use svd_vh(false) for compact row-wise principal directions in the input space. Use full mode only when the complete right null-space basis is needed, and joint svd() when directions must stay paired with scales and outputs.
